implementation.discoveryAndElection: Each install advertises a stable playerId, nickname, and protocol v2 over NSD. The lower lexicographic install UUID is the authority for that pair; users never enter addresses or ports. Both devices can originate a challenge through their authority direction.
implementation.challengeAndColor: A 30-second PENDING challenge is serialized in the authority SQLite store. The non-authority device applies to the authority, or the authority can offer a challenge to the higher-ID device. In both directions applicantId maps to whiteId and acceptorId maps to blackId; authority_id is stored separately.
implementation.authorityState: SQLiteOpenHelper tables: lan_players, lan_challenges, lan_games, lan_moves, lan_requests. A single synchronized transaction checks deadlines/permissions/revision, writes state and successful request records, and commits before response snapshots are published.
implementation.movePath: Both local host moves and remote requests call LanGameRepository.handle with requestId/expectedRevision/x/y. Only committed snapshots replace board stones; request replay returns the current snapshot and request payload conflicts are rejected.
implementation.nicknameScope: NFKC/trim, 2-12 grapheme, letters/marks/numbers/_/-, reserved-name rejection, atomic guestN allocation; normalized names are unique in the authority device database. Other authority databases are separate scopes.
implementation.gameClock: The authority persists a 60-second turn deadline and checks it every 250ms; timeout state and a system success record are committed together.

limitations: A LAN authority uses plain TCP JSON; it is not encrypted and does not provide public-Internet security.
An Activity/process kill stops its host service; automatic host migration and post-process reconnection are not implemented here.
LAN chat, rematch, PNG save/share, and the full PWA result-room policy remain separate integration work.
